findings.conclusion: Initial RunTask, DescribeTasks include TAGS, and ListTagsForResource exposed the merged definition/request tags; explicit request value won the overlap.
Task tag mutation and removal were reflected by DescribeTasks include TAGS, ListTagsForResource, and exact-token RunTask replay; replay returned mutable task tags, not immutable admission tags.
Subsequent definition tag changes did not change existing task tags or replay tags in this sequence.

Changing only cluster from its original name to the equivalent ARN with the same token returned HTTP 400 ConflictException with resourceIds containing the original task ARN; baseline replay immediately afterward still succeeded. No extra task was admitted.

StopTask returned tags=[]; after STOPPED, DescribeTasks include TAGS and exact-token replay retained the mutated task tags. ListTagsForResource returned HTTP 400 InvalidParameterException with message: The specified task is stopped. Specify a running task and try again.

Exact original token/request replay failed after deregistration with HTTP 400 InvalidParameterException: TaskDefinition is inactive. With DELETE_IN_PROGRESS it failed with HTTP 400 InvalidParameterException: TaskDefinition is being deleted. Thus observed definition eligibility errors take precedence over returning the already-known task in these states.

Only one distinct task ARN appeared in successful RunTask responses; explicit StopTask was requested approximately 13.4 seconds after initial RunTask request began. No RUNNING task status was observed.

executionNote: Initial Python eval kernel terminated during bounded STOPPED wait after explicit StopTask. Continued from persisted observations with a finite recovery process and finally cleanup; no admission sequence repeated.
unresolved: Replay after final definition disappearance was not tested; definition deletion was requested successfully and DELETE_IN_PROGRESS observed.
No token-expiry, RUNNING-container, or delayed propagation investigation was performed; all tag/replay conclusions are scoped to this short-window sequence.
